sections.title: What hooks are

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: Your PDFs do not cover this topic, so this page was written for the site. Your 12-week plan lists React, hooks, rendering, performance, state management and TypeScript. Check it against the official documentation, or give me a PDF to replace it.

blocks: Hooks are functions that let a component keep state and run side effects. React identifies each hook by **its call order**, so there are two rules: call them only at the top level of a component or custom hook, and never inside conditions or loops.

blocks.title: Effect lifecycle
blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  A[Component renders] --> B[React updates the DOM]
  B --> C[Browser paints]
  C --> D{Did a dependency change?}
  D -->|first render or yes| E[Run cleanup of the previous effect]
  E --> F[Run the effect]
  D -->|no| G[Skip]
  H[Component removed] --> I[Run cleanup]
blocks.caption: Effects run after paint. Cleanup runs before the next run and on removal.

blocks.title: Fetching with cleanup

walkthrough.title: Cancellable request
walkthrough.text: The controller lets the cleanup cancel this request.

walkthrough.title: Cleanup
walkthrough.text: If `id` changes quickly, the old request is cancelled, so a slow old response cannot overwrite the new one. This bug is called a race condition.

walkthrough.title: Dependencies
walkthrough.text: The effect reruns when `id` changes. List everything from the component that the effect uses.

blocks.title: You might not need an effect
blocks.text: Do not use an effect to compute a value from props or state: calculate it during render. `const fullName = first + ' ' + last` needs no state and no effect. Effects are for synchronising with things outside React.

blocks.title: Strict Mode
blocks.text: In development, `StrictMode` runs each effect, its cleanup and the effect again on mount, to expose missing cleanups. Two requests in development are expected, not a bug.

sections.title: The stale closure
blocks: Each render has its own props and state values. A function created during a render closes over that render's values forever.

sections.title: Custom hooks
blocks: A custom hook is a function starting with `use` that calls other hooks. It shares logic, not state: each component that calls it gets its own copy.

blocks.title: useFetch.ts
Interview angle
blocks.text: **Why can't hooks be called conditionally?** React stores hook state in a list per component and matches it by call position. A conditional call shifts the positions, so hooks read each other's state.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Call hooks at the top level only.
- Effects synchronise with the outside world; do not use them to derive values.
- Always return a cleanup for subscriptions, timers and requests.
- List every dependency the effect uses.
- Use the updater form `setX((x) => ...)` when the new value depends on the old one.

items.question: Why does a request fire twice in development?
items.answer: StrictMode mounts, cleans up and remounts in development to reveal missing cleanups. It does not happen in production.

items.question: What is the difference between `useRef` and `useState`?
items.answer: Changing a ref does not re-render and takes effect immediately. Setting state schedules a re-render.

items.question: What is a stale closure, and how do you fix one?
items.answer: A function keeps the values from the render that created it. Fix it by listing the dependency or using the updater form of the setter.

items.question: How does a custom hook differ from a shared service in Spring?
items.answer: A Spring singleton shares one instance and its state. A custom hook shares only the logic: each component gets separate state.
